note:
Closes the one real functional gap left in landmarks.js's statue system after LandmarkPlacer.cs (HeroStatueDef/Tint/PlaceWorld/BuildPedestal, 505 lines already claimed): no Unity Material for Gold/Aluminum/BronzeV/street-tint/bust-tint was ever built anywhere, so LandmarkPlacer.Tint was inert data with nothing to render. Ports: GOLD (landmarks.js:63, MeshStandardMaterial 0xd9b13b metalness.85 roughness.25 -- the gilded St George), ALUMINUM (1219, 0xc9ccd1 .75/.35 -- Kartlis Deda), BRONZE_V (1222, 0xfff6ea .45/.55 -- rustaveli/david/nino/vazha/writer_ilia/writer_akaki/pharnavaz), streetMat (1498, 0xcbb89a -- the 207-point instanced street-statue layer) and bustMat (1504, 0xbfae92 -- the 91-point bust layer), plus statueGLB()'s per-mesh traverse (1227-1250: castShadow=true always; material overridden unless the JS passes null, which happens for gorgasali/saakadze to keep their photogrammetry scan's own baked texture -- Tint.KeepOwn). StatueMaterials.For(Tint) and ApplyToInstance(GameObject,Tint) are the two call points a scene-bake step needs; LandmarkPlacer.cs itself was not edited.

NOT PORTED, on purpose: landmarks.js:1216-1217's module-level BRONZE (0x5a4a38) and PATINA (0x4f7a68) consts -- neither is referenced by any of the ten statue builder functions (freedomMonument..pharnavaz), confirmed by tools/_probe_landmarksrest.mjs's CONST_USED_IN_STATUES check (both 0). They are dead code in the live game; porting them would reproduce something nothing calls. (philharmonic()'s own local `const PATINA = lambert(0x5f8f7a)` is an unrelated value belonging to that landmark's own already-exported OBJ asset, not this file.)

KNOWN LIMITATION, reported rather than guessed at: three of these materials set `vertexColors: true` in the JS -- BRONZE_V reads a real per-vertex patina mask baked into the statue FBX by tools/build_statues2.py (COLOR_0), and streetMat/bustMat do the same for their instanced variants. Unity's stock URP/Lit shader does not sample mesh vertex colour at all, and there is no project-wide solution for this yet anywhere in the Unity port -- WorshipPlacer.cs's own header states the identical gap ('a future pass can drop real photo materials on... with nothing but a vertex-colour material assigned'). The materials built here carry every OTHER JS parameter correctly (base colour, metallic, smoothness) so the statues read right at a glance; closing the vertex-colour gap itself needs a custom/Shader-Graph shader that is bigger than one file and was not invented speculatively without the ability to run the editor and check it actually renders.
verified: tools/_probe_landmarksrest.mjs, RUN directly (node tools/_probe_landmarksrest.mjs): regexes GOLD/ALUMINUM/BRONZE_V/streetMat/bustMat's literal color+metalness+roughness straight out of the live src/landmarks.js source text (not retyped), and every statueGLB('<file>', <mat>, ...) call argument for all 10 heroes (george=GOLD, kartlis_deda=ALUMINUM, gorgasali=null, rustaveli/david/nino/vazha/writer_ilia/writer_akaki/pharnavaz=BRONZE_V, saakadze=null) -- output pasted in the task report, matches StatueMaterials.cs's constants and Tint mapping exactly, 0 mismatches. Also confirms BRONZE/PATINA are unused (CONST_USED_IN_STATUES n=0 for both) and that addStorefronts/peaceBridge/ship are each called exactly once -- their own declaration, i.e. never actually invoked (CALL_SITES n=1 for all three), backing the 'dead code, not ported' claim in landmarks.json's existing note. Assets/Editor/Probes/LandmarksRestProbe.cs mirrors the same STATMAT/STATUE_MAT checks by reading the built Materials back (color/metallic/smoothness round-trip) and exercises ApplyToInstance on a synthetic renderer hierarchy (Gold swaps the material and forces shadows on; KeepOwn leaves the original material) -- written but NOT run (no editor access, a batch-mode lock is held elsewhere per the task brief); only the Node side was executed.

note:
Closes the other gap in LandmarkPlacer.cs's justice-house entry: BuiltLandmarks's 'იუსტიციის სახლი' row (AssetPath=Assets/Art/Props/justice_house.fbx) is placement data only (position+yaw from GeoFrame), never a traverse over the imported prefab's renderers. Ports justiceHouse()'s post-load fixup block verbatim (landmarks.js:1370-1381, the body of gltf.scene.traverse): every mesh gets castShadow=true and receiveShadow=true; every material that is ALREADY transparent (the glazing) gets depthWrite=false so it doesn't sort in front of the petals it sits under; envMapIntensity=0.6 is attempted on every material. Call ApplyFixups(GameObject) once after the FBX is instantiated at LandmarkPlacer.PlaceWorld(def)'s transform.

NOT PORTED, on purpose: the outer `newGltfLoader().load('models/justice_house.glb', ...)` call and its error callback (landmarks.js:1369,1383) -- Unity substitutes this with its own FBX import (already wired via LandmarkPlacer.AssetPath, same as every other BuiltLandmarks entry), so there is no runtime network/load-failure path to reproduce.

KNOWN LIMITATION, reported rather than guessed at: `envMapIntensity = 0.6` (Three.js MeshStandardMaterial, a continuous 0..1+ reflection-strength scalar) has no URP/Lit equivalent -- the stock shader exposes only an Environment Reflections ON/OFF toggle (_EnvironmentReflections), not an intensity float, so there is no property to write 0.6 into. Left unset rather than approximated with an unverifiable guess (no batch-mode render available to check it against). Separately, URP's Lit shader already sets ZWrite Off for Surface Type=Transparent as part of its own standard transparent setup, so the depthWrite fix this file applies is PROBABLY already a no-op in practice -- reproduced anyway because it is an exact, harmless 1:1 mirror of the JS guard (only ever touches a material that is already transparent).
verified: tools/_probe_landmarksrest.mjs, RUN directly: regexes landmarks.js's literal `m.envMapIntensity = 0.6;` (JUSTICE_ENV_MAP_INTENSITY value=0.6), confirms the `if (m && m.transparent) m.depthWrite = false;` guard text is present verbatim (JUSTICE_DEPTHWRITE_GUARD present=1), and confirms the castShadow/receiveShadow pair precedes it in source order (JUSTICE_SHADOW_FIXUPS present=1) -- all three match JusticeHouseMaterials.cs's doc comments and behaviour. Assets/Editor/Probes/LandmarksRestProbe.cs builds a synthetic hierarchy with one opaque and one deliberately-wrong-ZWrite transparent URP/Lit material, calls ApplyFixups, and checks the transparent one's _ZWrite flips to 0 while the opaque one is left alone, plus both renderers' shadow/receive flags -- written but NOT run (no editor access); only the Node-side regex checks above were executed.
